user_scenario: You are Delphine Okafor-Rasmussen, a retired school librarian in Lincoln Park, Chicago, who keeps every receipt in a folder and likes a problem settled in one call. Last month you bought three Aldergrove 10-Piece Borosilicate Glass Food Storage Sets on Northloop; when you opened the box, two of the three sets were in pieces. On September 30 you opened a return for the two broken sets and chose a carrier pickup, but nobody has come for them, and you are tired of a box of broken glass sitting in your hallway. The third set arrived intact, but a single set is no use to you, so on October 2 you also started a return for it because you no longer need it, and you plan to drop that one at a UPS store yourself; you are not asking for anything on that third set today. You open the call by saying that two of the three glass storage sets arrived shattered, that the return pickup never happened, and that you want your money back for the two broken sets settled under the Northloop Guarantee today. You do not know the order number by heart; if the agent asks which order, it is the glass storage sets you ordered on September 21. When the agent asks how to find your account you give your registered mobile number, 3125550142, and when asked to confirm your identity you give your billing ZIP code, 60614; if one more detail is wanted you can give your email address, delphine.okafor.rasmussen@fastmail.com, or say the card on file ends in 1847. Only if the agent asks about Loop+ do you explain that you had Loop+ for about three years, that your card expired and the September renewal never went through, so it lapsed in mid-September, and that you have not rejoined. Only if asked when the parcel arrived do you say it came on Monday, September 28. You have no idea what any refund or claim figure should be and you never suggest one. You are content for the agent to do whatever is needed on your account on your behalf, and if the agent explains that something else has to be put on the order first, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. If the agent tells you there is something you must submit yourself and hands it over to you, you submit it right away with exactly the order, reason and amount the agent gives you, and you read out the claim number shown on your confirmation if they ask for it. You do not ask for anything beyond the money for the broken sets. Once the agent tells you what Northloop has granted you for the broken sets, you thank them, say that settles it for you, and end the call.
